No coordinate is discarded without its total-one identity.

The actual balanced average keeps eta_p=p*1_{p|z_u} outside the bounded test. After coordinate-u dilation its test is exactly the coordinate-v inserted test, by nonzero-prime division cancellation. The test H at the balanced coordinates is still bounded by V^B on every integer tuple, so no p<=V premise or unquantified error multiplied by a growing prime is introduced.

The balanced error is the sum of the derived v-coordinate prime-average insertion cap and the u-coordinate V^B fixed-prime dilation cap. Exact Fubini with the original fresh-prime mass integrates the fixed-prime estimate. Both limits are derived from existing actual master scale growth, and the final bound is uniform over all tests at each stage for every fixed natural B.

The actual fresh-prime off-diagonal expectation equals the original tensor-prime expectation of the original shared outer mean, with the p!=q indicator retained. Applying the actual stage fixed-pair transfer on supported p,q yields abs(V^B*dilationCap) as a uniform error. The original tensor law has total one; the off-diagonal part is neither normalized nor treated as an independent resampling of old tuples.

For a supported distinct fresh-prime pair, the two eta multipliers equal eta_{pq}. Absorbing them by original harmonic dilation changes the two balanced coordinate maps exactly into (q,p) and (p,q). Fresh-prime support supplies p!=0 and q!=0. The equality is only needed on that support and is extended to the actual averages by the support-congruence theorem.

The concrete two-branch bound currently concerns arbitrary branch tests H(r,p) globally bounded in the coordinates on the original old-prime/fresh-prime support. Their product is bounded by V^(2B), proved directly. The generic off-diagonal absorption also admits any pair-dependent polynomially bounded integrand. These results have not yet been identified with the full row-weight-normalized integrand containing the single invariant density Omega.
